profile.reading:
This building, mapped as NTT Chicago CH3, sits at 235 East Pierce Road, Itasca, IL 60143, part of the same Itasca, DuPage County campus as NTT's CH1 (255 Pierce Rd) and CH2 (275 Pierce Rd) buildings. Unlike CH1 and CH2, NTT does not publish an individual facility page for CH3, so this entry's address is drawn from public geocoded property data rather than an operator-confirmed page, and specific square footage or MW figures for this building could not be independently confirmed this session; that gap is stated plainly rather than estimated. NTT's own materials describe the combined Itasca campus, which the operator says includes four buildings (CH1 through CH4), as exceeding 200 megawatts of critical IT load in total; CH1 and CH2 alone account for 72 of those megawatts per NTT's own per-building pages, implying CH3 and CH4 together supply the balance.

Illinois's data center tax incentive program has become a flashpoint for state energy policy. Governor JB Pritzker announced on June 5, 2026 a temporary suspension of new awards under the state's Data Center Investment Program, citing grid strain; ComEd's CEO stated the program had added roughly $12 a month to the average residential bill over the prior four years. ComEd's northern Illinois service territory is separately projected to face capacity shortfalls beginning around 2029 as data center demand grows, according to legal-industry analysis of ComEd's planning filings.

NTT's US Global Data Centers footprint spans seven named campuses in total: Ashburn, Virginia at 224 megawatts; Chicago, Illinois at more than 200 megawatts; Dallas, Texas at 160 megawatts; Hillsboro, Oregon at 126 megawatts; Phoenix, Arizona at 240 megawatts; and a combined Sacramento/Santa Clara, California figure of 68 megawatts, totaling roughly 1,118 megawatts or more of disclosed US capacity, per the operator's own locations page. The US business operates under the NTT DATA Global Data Centers Americas name, the successor brand to RagingWire Data Centers, now under Japan's NTT DATA Group and parent Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corporation, a Tokyo Stock Exchange-listed company not subject to SEC 10-K filing requirements.

reading.body:
NTT's Chicago CH3 facility publishes 32 MW of IT capacity, making it the second-largest among six Illinois facilities with disclosed megawatts and accounting for roughly 14 percent of the 236 MW visible across those six sites.

Thirty-two megawatts of IT load translates to roughly 800 racks at 40 kW per rack, a density common in GPU-dense AI training deployments, or 3,200 racks at 10 kW per rack for conservative colocation. NTT does not publish the actual rack density for this facility, so these figures show the power's potential use rather than its current allocation. The facility sits in Illinois, a state where grid and land constraints have begun limiting new data center capacity, making existing megawatt allocations meaningful for understanding regional AI infrastructure density.

The published specifications list no certifications, so this data does not indicate whether the facility meets specific environmental or security standards. Illinois contains at least 44 mapped data center facilities total, but only six publish capacity figures, so 236 MW is a floor for the state's disclosed AI-ready infrastructure, not a full accounting. The location and scale indicate CH3 is large enough to host AI inference workloads or portions of a training cluster, but the data does not reveal current tenant uses or available power to new customers.
